newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far-right seen seizing fourth French town.
newsitem.headline: Far-right seen seizing fourth French town.

text.p: France's far-right National Front won a hard-fought municipal election on Sunday, taking to four the number of southern towns it controls, according to news media projections based on early returns.

French radio reported that first estimates showed Front candidate Catherine Megret, wife of the party's number two Bruno Megret, won 51.3 percent of the vote, against Socialist Jean-Jacques Anglade's 48.77 percent.

"Who can say that the National Front is not capable of becoming France's first party? If you judge from the Vitrolles microcosm, you realise that it's possible," Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen told Europe-1 radio shortly before the partial results were announced.

Megret won 46.7 percent of the vote in last Sunday's first round, boosting the anti-immigration movement's score in the town by four points since 1995. Her husband had been barred from running this time after a court found him guilty of campaign spending irregularities two years ago.
Anglade, who won re-election in 1995 by a mere 353 votes, took 37 percent last Sunday at the head of a united list of Socialists, Communists and ecologists on a 76 percent turnout.

Conservative candidate Roger Guichard scored 16.3 percent and pulled out of the second ballot at the insistence of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's centre-right national coalition, which urged a "republican vote to bar the road to the extreme-right".
